svg.text: A page’s audience rules are a log; its forms are rows
0376. The two tables under the seam 0359 clause 6 declared instead of a schema, and the one read that makes the log a record.
loom_audience_rules — APPENDED, ATTRIBUTED, THE WHOLE ORDERED LIST
REVISION RULES (IN ORDER) ACTOR
1 [aud_eu] person:ana
2 [aud_eu, aud_uk] person:ben
3 [aud_uk, aud_eu] person:ben
Revision 3 is the same two rules reordered, and it is an edit:
the order is the precedence, so a reorder changes who sees what.
history() is part of the contract, not a convenience.
The first draft kept every revision and no read reached past the head. A planted mutation that
overwrote the log instead of appending to it changed nothing any caller could see — the revision
numbers come off the head either way. 15 contract tests became 19, and the mutation died.
loom_audience_forms — ONE ROW PER AUDIENCE, REPLACED IN PLACE
AUDIENCE BASE_REVISION DELTA AUTHORED
aud_eu 4 jsonb 10 Nov 09:00
aud_uk 3 jsonb 08 Nov 17:20
base_revision is the one denormalised column, and it is
why forms() can say which form is behind the page
without loading a single delta.
A form is a document, not an event.
A base edit stales every audience delta, so rebasing one is the
ordinary thing that happens to it. A log of every rebase would
record drafting rather than deciding. No delete, either: an
audience stops being served by leaving the rules.
WHAT BUILDING IT PUT SIDE BY SIDE — FILED AS A QUESTION, NOT ANSWERED HERE
a change to the base
proposal → Gate → disposition → log
judged under a recorded policy
Leaves a revision, a proposal, a disposition and a
fingerprint. judgedUnder says which rules judged it.
a change to one audience’s form
setForm → row → composed at the next request
nothing judges it
Leaves the actor and the stamp on the row. Both columns
are what their own records decided — a form is
deliberately not a revision (0359 clause 4) — and they
reach a reader the same way.
audienceOverlaySourceFromStore
satisfies the seam. A deployment with no rules is served exactly what it is served today.
